These Families Get $10,000 If They Agree to A Data Center
 
Plus, how home buyers are strategizing around the new normal of high mortgage rates
 
By Craig Karmin
 

This is an edition of the Real Estate newsletter, a weekly briefing of the biggest commercial deals, news, analysis and trends in office, multifamily, retail and other commercial sectors. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

Imagine getting a direct cash payout if a developer builds a data center in your town. Residents of Hazle Township, Pa., are weighing this possibility now. A developer is offering $10,000 to every household if officials approve a new data center from Northpoint Development. For many in the township, which has a median household income of about $60,000, that kind of payout would be a significant sum. But regardless of income, job status or location, few of the people in Hazle Township have indicated that they are eager to welcome the data center for the payout. Reporter Will Parker visited the area and spoke to its residents about why.

 

Carnegie Mellon just became the recipient of the largest-ever individual donation to higher education. Hedge-fund billionaire Ken Griffin is giving the school $2 billion to help start a technology-focused Miami campus, along with an additional $1 billion for the university’s existing Pittsburgh campus. Carnegie Mellon Miami will focus on topics including biological discovery and national security. That fits right in with the region’s burgeoning defense tech and healthcare industries, Deborah Acosta reports.

 
 
 

Every Household in This Rural Town Receives $10,000 if a Data Center Gets Built

 
 
JOE LAMBERTI FOR WSJ
 

The letters started arriving in June, from a big developer who said he would give $10,000 to every family in Hazle Township, Pa. They could spend it on anything. They just needed to let NorthPoint Development build its data center, the first of 15 buildings the firm planned on 1,300 acres in the Pocono foothills.

 

Few of the people in Hazle Township interviewed by The Wall Street Journal indicated that they are eager to welcome the data center for the payout.

 
 
 
$45 Million
 

The amount that NorthPoint Development would pay if it gave every household in Hazle Township a $10,000 check.

Ken Griffin Is Making the Largest Donation to Higher Education in U.S. History

 
 
PATRICK T. FALLON/AGENCE FRANCE-PRESSE/GETTY IMAGES
 

Hedge-fund titan Ken Griffin is donating $2 billion to start a Carnegie Mellon University campus in Miami, part of the largest-ever individual gift toward higher education.

 

The Pittsburgh-based university, known for its expertise in computer science, artificial intelligence and robotics, will open a 35-acre campus in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood that will focus on technology and innovation.

 
 
 

Mayor Mamdani Must Redo New York City Pied-à-Terre Tax, Judge Says

 
 
MICHAEL NAGLE/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

New York City Mayor Mamdani must redo the rollout of his new pied-à-terre tax, a state judge ruled Tuesday, dealing a major blow to one of the mayor’s signature policies.

 

Separately, a lawsuit from two prominent businessmen—former Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross and casino mogul Steve Wynn—challenges the constitutionality of New York City’s pied-à-terre tax, in what they say is the first suit to allege that the tax is illegal.

 
 
 

Data Points

 

• $4,400: Median rent for a San Francisco one-bedroom in September, a record high and a 25.4% annual increase, according to Zumper. That is just $180 cheaper than in New York City—the narrowest that gap has been all year.

 

• 251,000: The number of open construction sector jobs in August, a 16% decline from July, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

 

• $205: The median price a square foot that new homes sold for in July, below the $212 median for existing homes, according to a Zillow analysis. From 2018 to 2024, new homes usually cost more a square foot than existing homes but that trend has reversed in recent years.
